description: We are two friends - a designer and a programmer, a humanities person and a techie. We are passionate about game dev, and we're looking forward to turning hard science into fun gameplay!
summary:
VOYAGER 1976 is a alternative-history narrative game. The Voyager Mars Program was successful - and first human crew was sent. Unfortunately, the base's costruction breaks down due to temperature swings. The crew has to evacuate to the Mars Ascent Vehicle (MAV). Since the Mothership is in a 5-Sol elliptical orbit, and MAV Delta-V is too low to reach it at apoapsis, they are forced to stay in the MAV for 120 hours - and survive.

The player should manage four critical systems in the gameplay loop:
1) Air control (through LiOH filters)
2) Power management (to survive the -100°C nights)
3) Manual radio tuning (to catch daily updates from the Mothership and Earth Mission Coordinator)
4) Extravehicular activity (to salvage parts and execute a final manual ignition checklist)

Target audience are children ages 7-12: VOYAGER 1976 transforms abstract aerospace physics into interactive experience (without heavy text).

VOYAGE 1976 is inspired by NASA missions (planned Voyager Mars Program, real Viking program) and Apollo-era analog engineering.
details:
What does VOYAGER 1976 do and how does it work?

-> it's a game to inform children about Mars and its environment, analogue technologies of 1970s, and survival mechanisms in space

VOYAGER 1976 starts with the "panic phase" - real-time 60 sec sequence; player must evacuate to the Mars Ascent Vehicle, choosing 2 out of 5 survival items. It predetermines the following game.

Main game loop is 120-hours survival inside the tiny rocket while managing four analog systems:

1) manually swapping LiOH filters to prevent CO2 toxicity

2) rerouting power to heaters to survive -100°C Martian nights

3) tuning radio frequencies through static to catch Earth updates

4) completing a sequential NASA ignition checklist for the final launch.

What benefits does VOYAGER 1976 have?

It translates aerospace concepts into gameplay. There is no heavy text. Players learn that space exploration isn't about magic technology, but about resource management, analog engineering, and working within the strict laws of physics.

What is the intended impact of the project?

To inspire the next generation of STEM enthusiasts.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

Gemini and ChatGPT for picture creating (all pictures are AI!)

ElevenLabs and Pixabay for audio generation/choise

Unity for game development

Gimp for video creation

How is your project creative?

VOYAGER 1976 is an alternative-history game, and it's narrative - unlike lots of sandbox games.

What factors did your team consider?

Target audience -> simplifying complex science without making it inaccurate

Scientific accuracy -> orbital mechanics, Delta-V limitations, and Martian weather conditions to ensure our narrative obstacles (why they must wait exactly 5 Sols, why the temperature drops) are rooted in real physics

Accessibility -> minimization of text, relying instead on visual cues (red alarms, frosting windows) and audio
